messages:
Maria K: Heads up — been seeing a few SLO breaches from long-tail 1-2 token requests when the continuous batcher is saturated. thinking about an escape-hatch that routes tiny, high-QPS tenants into ephemeral micro-queues (cohorts) rather than letting them starve the main coalesce window.
Sachin: +1 to an escape hatch. can we keep it simple: micro-queue per-cohort with a strict max inflight and no batching for tiny requests?
Leo: My worry: kv-cache pressure and cold-start penalties if we spin up micro-queues frequently. we need a TTL and a reuse strategy.
Julia: Proposal sketch: classify request as TINY if tokens<=8 and estimated latency-budget<=50ms. route TINY to cohort micro-queue which has two modes: coalesce-if-safe (join small microbatches up to N) or fastpath-serial (one-at-a-time) depending on instantaneous headroom.
Maria K: + the cohort should be tenant-aware so a noisy neighbor inside a cohort doesn't clobber others. use credit-based admission per-tenant inside the micro-queue.
Sachin: telemetry: emit cohort_load_factor and cohort_headroom_ms, so ops can tune N and serial threshold. also log when we fall back to serial so we can measure frequency.
Leo: Implementation concerns: this touches admission (where we check credits) and coalescer (where windows form). I think we should separate the admission API from the coalescer operator, with a tiny adapter layer that can choose micro-queue vs main queue. keeps boundaries cleaner.
Julia: Agree. Adapter API sketch: 
```
// AdmissionAdapter decides route
Route decide_route(Request r, AdmissionState s) {
  if (is_tiny(r) && cohort_headroom(s) < COHORT_THRESHOLD) return Route::SERIAL_FASTPATH;
  if (is_tiny(r)) return Route::MICRO_COHORT;
  return Route::MAIN_COALESCE;
}
```
Maria K: That code looks fine as a starting point. also need to handle rollback: if micro-cohort latency degrades, we should flow back to main queue or even to dedicated fastlane.
Sachin: One tradeoff: soft-preempt (throttle/bump priority) vs hard-preempt (drop from batch and re-enqueue). I prefer soft-preempt for predictable throughput; hard-preempt only for strict SLOs.
Leo: Also add metric for kv_cache_evictions caused_by_cohort to see if cohort churn hurts model cache hit rates.
Julia: Ops config example (suggested defaults): 
```
cohort: {
  tiny_token_threshold: 8,
  serial_threshold_ms: 30,
  max_microbatch_size: 4,
  cohort_ttl_s: 5
}
```
Maria K: Next steps: 1) PoC adapter that routes tiny traffic to an in-process micro-queue (no persistent infra), 2) emit new telemetry fields, 3) run chaos (noisy tenant) to validate isolation.
runtime-bot: deploy-preview created for branch "microcohort/adapt-router" — CI passed.
Sachin: I'll grab the PoC. tagging @Julia for coalescer changes and @Leo for kv-cache telemetry hooks.
Julia: I'll prototype the adapter interface and a tiny integration test that asserts route decisions under simulated load.
Leo: I'll add the kv-cache eviction counters and a Grafana tile for cohort impact.
Maria K: Thanks team. Let's sync in tomorrow standup; if PoC looks stable we can roll a canary behind a feature flag. :thumbsup:
